title: 2026-11-20 — A cargo-mutants `--output` written into a chunk's evidence carries host paths that hygiene refuses

data.head: ## 2026-11-20 — A cargo-mutants `--output` written into a chunk's evidence carries host paths that hygiene refuses

body:
cargo-mutants writes its run record into the `--output` directory's `mutants.out/`. `debug.log`, the `log/` directory
and `outcomes.json` there hold absolute host paths (the workspace root, the home dir). So when that directory is a
chunk's `evidence/`, `gate.py hygiene` refuses those files and `rec.py land` lands nothing.

The outcome lists carry no path: `caught.txt`, `missed.txt`, `timeout.txt`, `unviable.txt`, `mutants.json`,
`lock.json` and `diff/`. Keep them in evidence, quote the run's summary line in the pass record, and MOVE the three
raw records under the gitignored `target/` (deleting nothing) before landing. The alternative is to point `--output`
outside evidence and copy the outcome lists in.
Any later mutation run written into evidence meets the same refusal.

The session added two unit tests to the browser crate and changed no product behaviour, no public, crate-visible or IPC surface, no dependency, no schema and no gate.
The tests pin the private scene-render step of the browser's screenshot capture: it returns the viewport size at scale 1.0 (800 by 600) and the physical size at a hidpi scale of 2.0 (1280 by 720).
They sit out of line in a sibling file with the _tests suffix, declared as a cfg(test) module by path, under the existing convention for out-of-line unit tests.
It measured the 0.3.0 Epoch 6 audit's four surviving scene-render mutants as caught, under hand controls and then under a cargo-mutants run fired on the founder's word, after the run's filter was mended from an unanchored name to the anchored verb form.
A fifth mutant, the capture of the anyrender scene replaced with nothing, read missed outside the founder's word; it is carried as a residual and a next-version incubator line, with no work on it here.
Nothing was retired.

body_fields.name: Scoped mutation run filter anchored on the verb
body_fields.rule: A cargo-mutants run scoped to one function anchors its filter on the mutant name's verb, the replace verb then the function's name and a space, and its mutant listing is read first and must show exactly the mutants the run is meant to test.
body_fields.why: The filter is an unanchored regex over the whole mutant name, location included, so a bare function name matches other functions holding it as a substring.
body_fields.because: A run filtered on the bare function name tested a mutant outside its scope, and the mended filter anchored on the verb, checked by its listing first, is now the convention for scoped mutation runs.
